page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 375.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.72 GB per core. Graphics processing is handled by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The Intel Xeon CPU achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 62892.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 64768.69, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng score of 2209.29. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for read operations, reaching 4985.78 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 211.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec. The dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs demonstrate top-tier performance in LLM inference, processing 13643.47 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 6275.36 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

This server offers high resource density by combining substantial system memory, dual enterprise GPUs, and local NVMe storage on a single instance. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without virtualization overhead, though the 2.0 GHz base clock speed limits single-threaded performance compared to higher-frequency alternatives. Given the dual L40S GPUs and high-speed memory read bandwidth, this configuration is suited for large language model inference, machine learning training, database operations, and data-intensive processing workloads.
